definitions.explanation: A person who betrays the trust of others, whether in personal relationships, organizations, or political allegiances. Carries strong negative emotion.

examples.japanese: あいつは{裏切|うらぎ}り{者|もの}だ。
{仲間|なかま}の{中|なか}に{裏切|うらぎ}り{者|もの}がいた。
examples.english: There was a traitor among the group.

examples.japanese: {裏切|うらぎ}り{者|もの}と{呼|よ}ばれても、{自分|じぶん}の{信念|しんねん}を{貫|つらぬ}いた。
examples.english: Even though he was called a traitor, he stuck to his beliefs.

notes:
Composed of {裏切|うらぎ}り (betrayal; the noun form of {裏切|うらぎ}る) and {者|もの} (person). A highly emotional word used to label someone who has broken trust. Common in fiction (especially period dramas and thrillers) and in heated interpersonal or political disputes.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {裏切|うらぎ}り{者|もの}と{呼|よ}ぶ: to call someone a traitor
- {裏切|うらぎ}り{者|もの}を{許|ゆる}す: to forgive a traitor
- {裏切|うらぎ}り{者|もの}を{探|さが}す: to search for a traitor

RELATED WORDS:
- {裏切|うらぎ}る: to betray — the verb form
- {裏切|うらぎ}り: betrayal — the noun describing the act
- {反逆者|はんぎゃくしゃ}: rebel; insurgent — implies rebellion against authority rather than personal betrayal
- {売国奴|ばいこくど}: traitor to one's country — a much stronger and specifically political term
